oh-hd01-2026-jarrells-dontavius.name: Dontavius Jarrells
oh-hd01-2026-jarrells-dontavius.bio: State Representative for Ohio House District 1.

positions.stance: Says survivors deserve a future where "protection comes before tragedy, not after it," and backs his Break the Silence Act to support survivors in hospitals.
Voted against a 90-day gas tax holiday, saying relief should also reach groceries, utilities, property taxes and child-rearing costs.
Says economic growth should never come at the expense of clean water and backed individual permits for data center wastewater.
Supports library workers' right to organize, saying every worker deserves to be heard.
Championed a law letting schools store and administer naloxone to prevent overdose deaths among students and staff.

source.label: statements on their Ohio House office page

oh-hd03-2026-mohamed-ismail.name: Ismail Mohamed
oh-hd03-2026-mohamed-ismail.bio: State Representative for Ohio House District 3.

positions.stance: Says "every Ohioan deserves access to safe, stable housing" and backs permanent supportive housing to address chronic homelessness.
Opposes House Bill 347's 24-hour waiting period, calling it a violation of the reproductive rights voters approved in Issue 1.
Introducing legislation to restrict immigration enforcement at schools, hospitals, courthouses and places of worship.
Condemned the president's remarks about Somali immigrants and pledges to keep Ohio "a safe, welcoming home for all residents."
Calls SNAP benefits "a lifeline" and faulted the legislature for not acting to preserve them during the federal shutdown.

source.label: statements on their Ohio House office page

oh-hd05-2026-lawson-rowe-meredith.name: Meredith R. Lawson-Rowe
oh-hd05-2026-lawson-rowe-meredith.bio: State Representative for Ohio House District 5.

positions.stance: Supports relief at the pump but voted against House Bill 519's gas tax suspension, saying it addresses only part of the affordability crisis.
Welcomed $3.7 million for renovations at Rickenbacker Air National Guard Base to keep it a top military base.
Backs a bill creating 761st Tank Battalion Day to honor its service and remind Ohioans "how far we still have to go to ensure equality."
Supported capital budget funding for a Reynoldsburg food pantry, historic areas in Canal Winchester and recreation in south Columbus.
Sponsored a Cardiovascular Awareness Day to help Ohioans learn about heart health and healthy lifestyles.

source.label: statements on their Ohio House office page

oh-hd08-2026-hunter-kalagidis-kelly.name: Kelly Hunter-Kalagidis
oh-hd08-2026-hunter-kalagidis-kelly.bio: Former 16-year Columbus City Schools teacher now working in corporate supply chain operations.

positions.stance: Will focus on academic fundamentals, support teachers and ensure every student gets a high-quality education that prepares them for real jobs.
Supports complete curriculum transparency and says school districts should work with parents, not around them.
Will fight to cap unfair property tax spikes that are pricing families and seniors out of their homes.

oh-hd09-2026-euans-bruce.name: Bruce Euans
oh-hd09-2026-euans-bruce.bio: Businessman with a background in design/build, real estate, retail and business management.

positions.stance: Strongly supports law enforcement and policies that "equip, protect, and respect our officers."
Stands with active-duty military, veterans and their families, calling for proper resources, quality health care and opportunities at home.
Will push for stronger safeguards and oversight against fraud, waste and abuse in government spending.
Supports the Health and Human Services levy to fund services for children, older adults, behavioral health and addiction treatment.
Expressed full confidence in local elections and said any attempt to intimidate residents from voting "is wrong."

source.label: statements on the Cuyahoga County Executive's website

nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-stogo.name: Kyle Stogoski
nc-wake-2026-commissioner-at-large-stogo.bio: Southwest Raleigh resident who has worked rideshare and customer-facing hourly jobs.

positions.stance: Supports fast-track starter housing, down payment assistance for Wake residents, and limits on corporate buyers of single and multifamily homes.
Favors a local-business-first economy with small-business grants and permit streamlining, balanced by protections for farmland and open space.
Supports zero-based budgeting, public performance dashboards, independent audits and sunset clauses for programs that fail expectations.

mi-sbe-2026-pritchett-judith.name: Judith Pritchett
mi-sbe-2026-pritchett-judith.bio: Retired public school educator and administrator, elected to the State Board of Education in 2018.

positions.stance: Listed improving student achievement in Michigan as a top priority in her 2018 survey.
Listed supporting and respecting all education staff in the state as a top priority.
Listed "high and equitable opportunities for all students" as a top priority.
Says public education is under attack by those who want to close community schools or send outside emergency managers or CEOs to run them.
Says his administration focuses on improving infrastructure, promoting public safety, expanding recreation and fostering economic growth.

source.label: their Essex County Executive office page
